title: Heritability of Intelligence
summary: Nature vs Nurture, Phenotype and Genotype, Heritability research methods (Plomin's techniques), Environmental Influences on Intelligence.
objectives: Describe the nature vs nurture debate.
revision: Nature vs Nurture: genetic vs environmental influences on intelligence. Genotype = genes; Phenotype = observable traits. Heritability research: twin, adoption, family studies. Environment: nutrition, education, SES, family, early childhood.
traps: Heritability = proportion of population variation due to genetic differences.
confusions: Confusing heritability of a trait in a population with genetic determination of an individual.
Believing heritability is fixed across environments.

notes.t: The nature vs nurture debate concerns the relative contributions of genetic inheritance (nature) and environmental factors (nurture) to intelligence.
Genotype: genetic makeup. Phenotype: observable characteristics resulting from genotype and environment interaction.
Plomin's techniques for studying heritability include twin studies, adoption studies, and family studies.
Environmental factors affecting intelligence include nutrition, education, socioeconomic status, family environment, and early childhood experiences.
UGC NET frequently asks about heritability research methods and environmental influences on intelligence.
